methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Uptool operates in Robotics & Manufacturing at an undisclosed stage. The comparable universe consists of one public company (277810.KQ) and eight private peers, including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. This comp set reflects the fragmented nature of frontier-tech robotics, where stage and valuation tier heterogeneity complicate direct benchmarking.

Standard peer-median valuation methodology is not applicable here. The analysis identified 11 same-sector peers in Robotics & Manufacturing, but filtering for stage-aligned, tier-aligned, or adjacent-stage comparables yielded fewer than three datapoints in any narrow cohort. A full-sector median would obscure material differences in technology maturity, capital intensity, and revenue stage across the peer set and therefore was rejected as misleading.

Without sufficient triangulation via peer multiples, alternative methods—such as DCF modeling or precedent transaction analysis—would be required to establish a defensible valuation range. The current analysis cannot responsibly recommend a specific valuation absent either: (1) disclosure of Uptool's stage and financial metrics (revenue, burn, unit economics) to enable tighter peer matching, or (2) access to comparable transaction data or management projections. Key uncertainties include the target's commercialization timeline, capital requirements, and competitive positioning relative to the named private peers.
